device: 2x2 adiabatic directional coupler (symmetric arms, two parallel guides)

spec_optimization_harness_as_briefed.note: Two known-inapplicable checks, recorded verbatim for the audit: (a) delta_length is MZI-shaped - a symmetric coupler's arm delta is 0 identically, so no knob can move it; (b) its area numbers read 0.0 because spec_optimization._layer_area uses gdstk top_level(), which the gdsfactory $$$CONTEXT_INFO$$$ metadata cell defeats (it references every cell). The conductor gate's _layer_area handles that quirk and measures the same GDS pair at 85.643 -> 88.693 um^2.

gap_knob_geometric_response.note: gap knob moves centerlines, not area; verified against the written GDS at the taper midpoint

reading: coupling_length extends TWO parallel guides, so d(area)/d(knob) = (w_top_mid + w_bot_mid) = 0.61 um: the gate check passes exactly with width_um=0.61 and reads 2x the single-guide expectation with width_um=0.305 - that factor-2 is itself quantitative proof both guides respond. The MZI-shaped delta_length check cannot pass for a symmetric coupler (delta = 0 identically); the coupler's function knobs are verified by area (length) and measured-gap (gap) responses instead.
